newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujitsu says Amdahl buyout to cut its 97/98 profit.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu says Amdahl buyout to cut its 97/98 profit.

text.p: Fujitsu Ltd said on Thursday that its planned buyout of U.S. computer maker Amdahl Corp will reduce its 1997/98 group profit by about 1.5 billion yen due to a write-off of goodwill costs, Fujitsu Executive Vice President Takashi Maruyama told a news conference.
Fujitsu estimates Amdahl-related goodwill costs at about $500 million, which Fujitsu plans to write off in about 10 years.
Maruyama said, however, that Fujitsu currently has no plan to revise its group earnings estimates or capital investment programme for the current business year as a result of the Amdahl buyout.
He also said that about half of the approximately 100 billion yen purchase price for Amdahl will be covered by borrowing, while the rest will be covered by internal cash flow.
Fujitsu has not decided yet whether the borrowed funds will come from bank lending or from the issuance of straight bonds, Maruyama said.

He added that the buyout was proposed in late June by Amdahl executives, who were concerned about short-term problems with the company's performance. "They said the best way to eliminate their worries and ensure their customers of the company's good health was to get strong backing from Fujitsu," Maruyama said.

Asked if Fujitsu would be willing to raise its offer price of $12 per share for Amdahl if there is insufficient response from shareholders to its tender, Maruyama said Amdahl's share price had remained below $10 for a long time and at $12 the company has already offered a high premium.

Maruyama said Amdahl's strong customer base in the United States, its sales support systems and its ability to provide solution services will yield benefits for Fujitsu in its global computer hardware and software businesses.

Fujitsu and Amdahl announced on Wednesday that, pursuant to a definitive merger agreement, Fujitsu would purchase for $12 a share in cash all outstanding shares of Amdahl not currently owned by Fujitsu, with a total cost of about $850 million.
Fujitsu currently owns approximately 42 percent of Amdahl's shares.
